newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire Airlines halts flights to diamond city.
newsitem.headline: Zaire Airlines halts flights to diamond city.

text.p: Zaire Airlines, which serves Zaire's mining provinces, suspended flights to the diamond capital of Mbuji-Mayi on Friday, blaming problems with unruly soldiers, aviation sources said.

The soldiers, who retreated to the capital of the diamond mining province of Kasai after rebels took Kindu to the northeast, had been trying to force their way onto flights to Zaire's capital Kinshasa, the sources told Reuters.
The rebels, fighting to topple ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko since October, have named Mbuji-Mayi as one of their next major targets.
The sources also said that central government officials in Lubumbashi, capital of the copper and cobalt-mining province to the south, were putting their families on flights to Kinshasa.
But the officials themselves appeared to be staying put, the sources and members of the expatriate community said.
The rebels have named Lubumbashi, Zaire's second city, as another target.
Zaire Airlines was formed about a month ago after a merger between Zaire Express and Shabair. Zaire Express was a joint venture between the government and the Belgian airline Sabena.
Zaire Airlines runs a service from Kinshasa to Mbuji-Mayi and Lubumbashi. It is the main commercial service to Mbuji-Mayi but smaller airlines and charters fly in.
The airline sources said they did not know how long the flights would remain halted.
